children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'd like to ask about - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives with me at home. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask: Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training course)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually just left school recently. He's signed up with the local careers service though - he's trying to figure out what he wants to do next, whether that's college or getting a job or something else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know. 

To clarify the timeline - approximately how long ago did Alex leave school, and how long has he been registered with the careers service?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been quite recent - just a few weeks ago that he finished school, and he registered with the careers service pretty much straight away after that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
3. Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. 

No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me who's responsible for him.

And no, he's not working at all at the moment - he's just been focusing on sorting out his next steps. He's not claiming any benefits either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Since Alex is 16 and has registered with the government-sponsored careers service immediately after leaving school, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for up to **20 weeks** from when he left education.

### Important things to note:

- This 20-week period gives Alex time to decide on his next steps, whether that's further education, training, or employment
- The eligibility will stop if Alex starts working 24 hours or more per week, or if he starts claiming certain benefits in his own right
- If Alex returns to approved education or training (like college) before the 20 weeks are up, your Child Benefit could continue beyond the 20 weeks as long as he remains in that approved education/training and is under 20 years old

Make sure you inform HMRC if Alex's circumstances change during this period, such as if he starts work, begins an apprenticeship, or enrolls in college.

He is not working 24 hours or more per week, and he is not claiming benefits in his own right. You live with Alex in the UK, are responsible for him, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him, and you meet the residence requirements. Therefore, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex for up to 20 weeks from when he left education.
